$comment: Non-secret deployment configuration for StudioCRM. Committed on purpose: none of it is
sensitive. Every credential — the GitHub token, DATABASE_URL, JWT_SECRET, the FTP password,
the deploy hook URL — stays OUT of this file and out of git. See docs/DEPLOYMENT.md.
The host runs Node apps as a Linux container built from a GIT CLONE, not as an IIS site.
That was established from the host's own build log, not assumed. Anything in here that
reads like an FTP upload target is for reading logs, not for deploying.
Values marked TODO must be read from the SmarterASP.NET / Site4Now control panel. Do not
guess them: a wrong appUrl makes the health check pass against nothing.

panel.$deployTarget: What the panel's Node app page shows as the deploy target for this site.

git.$branch: The branch the panel clones. NOT main: origin/main predates the whole Masters / Appointments / Billing layer, so deploying main would deploy none of the app.
git.$auth: The repository is PRIVATE, so the panel needs a GitHub Personal Access Token with read access to it. The token is pasted into the panel by hand and is never stored here, in git, or in any script.

build.$command: Explicit, because the panel's npm default cannot resolve this repo's workspace:* dependencies, and because --prod=false keeps the devDependencies the web build needs even if NODE_ENV=production is set during install.
build.$start: Runs apps/api/dist/server.js — the single bundle that serves /api and the React build.

$appUrl: The public https:// URL of the site, used as the client-review link and as the base for verification. Control panel -> Websites -> Domains (the live domain, or the temporary URL the panel lists for this site).

logs.$why: FTPS over port 21 (the server's own FEAT advertises AUTH TLS). The site root is where the host drops its deploy log, node_app_automate_deploy_<id>.log — the only channel there is for reading why a container build failed. Nothing is DEPLOYED over FTP; files copied here do not become the running container.
